summary: Hardening review passed for the exact v0.3.43 candidate. A fresh disposable repository was bound before model execution to explicit paths, Codex worker profiles, a shared budget, a local bare Git publication target and no deployment authority. One controller run used real workers to materialize, verify, commit and publish two dependent tasks as v1.2.0 and v1.3.0, survived an injected SIGTERM after the first remote tag, waited for the interrupted worker group and resumed without manual per-task dispatch. The manifest records 437.987 elapsed seconds, zero human interventions, seven observed usage records, clean final Git state, exact local/remote commits, preserved goal/vision/architecture links and an achieved goal audit. Six failed attempts remain immutable evidence and exposed test collection coupling, overbroad selectors, unfrozen intake verification, cache pollution, ignored-cache release failure and a worker-drain race; each was repaired without weakening product gates. Static mutation tests reject false proof, exact-candidate completion checks pass, and a Linux release candidate passed 156 compatibility tests, 26 injected-failure autonomy tests and 197 smoke tests. Documentation deliberately limits the claim to this measured synthetic local-Git run: it does not claim eight hours, production deployment, private-pilot mutation, broad model quality or billing/identity attestation. Publication and official-origin readback remain the downstream release gate; no blocking finding remains.
